  `projectPath` resolves against the project root. This repo dogfoods it:
  `.fah/config.yaml` points at the COMMITTED `memory/` directory — clone
  the repo, get its memory. Inside the store dir: `MemoryRepoInit.
  ensureGitSupport()` (flutter_agent_memory 0.2.0) keeps `.gitignore`
  (derived artifacts: GRAPH.md, MEMORY.revision, INDEX.md,
  .last_maintenance — rebuilt on load, never committed) and
  `.gitattributes` (`DELETIONS.md merge=union` — the append-only
  tombstone ledger merges by union). Note ids are merge-friendly since
  0.2.0: `n_0447_a1b2` = sequential index + 4-hex md5 of the normalized
  text (parallel branches union-merge; legacy `n_0001` ids stay valid
  forever). The `memory_add` description IS the package's
  `MemoryPolicy.memoryAddPolicy` (docs/memory/memory_add_policy.md in
  the memory repo): durable facts only, solved problems are superseded
  via delete+add (never left to rot), project scope is PUBLIC (git) —
  no secrets/personal data there, user scope stays machine-local.
  `.gitignore` whitelists `.fah/config.yaml` (+rules/lsp/mcp/agents/
  skills/packages); logs/sessions/bash_jobs stay local. Commit memory/
  changes with the task that produced them (`memory:` prefix for
  memory-only commits).
- `lib/src/a2a/` — A2A (Agent2Agent) interop: `a2a_client.dart` (Agent Card
  + JSON-RPC + SSE), `a2a_config.dart` (`a2a:` yaml section, `${NAME}`
  env tokens), `a2a_manager.dart` (lazy per-server connect, A2A task state
  → subagent lifecycle mapping), `a2a_server.dart` (request handler).
  `task` tool agent type `a2a:<name>` runs remote agents as subagents
  (uniform `task_status`/`task_send`); `/a2a` shows server status;
  `fa serve --a2a [--port N] [--token T]` mounts this agent as an endpoint
  (`bin/serve_a2a.dart`).
- `lib/src/cli/hep.dart` + `agent_cli_hep_io.dart` — HEP v1, the Harness
  Event Protocol (`fa --output events[=full]`, issue #155): strict JSONL
  on stdout for server-side supervisors, one JSON object per line,
  flushed per line. A TURN is one assistant LLM ROUND, not one user
  message — a user turn that runs tools yields SEVERAL terminal frames
  (`turn_done` per round, ids incrementing). `HepWriter` is
  `AgentListener`-shaped (`agent.subscribe(hep.handleEvent)`); the
  `HepEventsIO` decorator (a `part of agent_cli.dart`) drops
  `CliIO.write` so stdout stays pure while diagnostics keep stderr.
  Frame catalog, ordering/flush guarantees and versioning policy:
  docs/hep.md; byte shape pinned by golden tests (test/cli/hep_test.dart).
  `--attach` sniffs image mimes by magic bytes (png/jpeg/gif/webp ride
  as base64 blocks); any other file passes through as an
  `[attached file: …]` path reference appended to the prompt (issue
  #196) — never an octet-stream image block.
- `bin/fah.dart` — the `fah`/`fa` CLI. REPL (no args) or headless
  (`fa "prompt"` / `-p` / `--prompt-file <path>` (alias `-f`), mutually
  exclusive). First positional naming an EXISTING file is the prompt source
  (`.md`/`.txt` inlined, others attached by reference; `-p` is verbatim;
  `--prompt-file` reads ANY path verbatim, missing/unreadable = usage
  error exit 64). Args parsed in `lib/src/cli/cli_args.dart`
  (pure Dart). Headless: exit 0/1/130; `CliIO` contract — `write` = primary
  stream, `writeln` = diagnostics (stderr headless). The TUI captures the
  mouse by default (wheel scrolling + click routing — the alternate screen

  works via the terminal's bypass modifier (Shift), and `FA_TUI_MOUSE=0`

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow
    detection via error-message regexes.
  - **Invariant to preserve: providers never throw.** All failures —
    network, 429, abort, malformed SSE — arrive as an `error` event with
    `stopReason: error|aborted`. The agent loop never sees an exception from
    a provider.
- `packages/agent/` (~8.1k LOC TS):
  - `packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts` (748 LOC) — the low-level async loop;
    port its shape, not its incidental JS-isms.
  - `packages/agent/src/agent.ts` (557 LOC) — stateful `Agent` with
    **steering / follow-up queues** (inject user messages mid-run — this is
    first-class behavior we must keep) and hooks (`beforeToolCall`,
    `afterToolCall`, `transformContext`, `prepareNextTurn`).
  - session layer — sessions as an **append-only JSONL tree** of records
    (branching, labels). Flat linear history is not acceptable.
  - compaction pipeline (~760 LOC) — `estimateTokens` (chars/4 heuristic,
    images ≈ 1200 tokens) → `shouldCompact` (reserve 16384 tokens) →
    `findCutPoint` (keep ~20k recent tokens) → `generateSummary` via LLM with
    a fixed structured prompt. Token-based, never message-count-based.
  - `ExecutionEnv` abstraction (FileSystem + Shell) — our portability
    boundary: default implementation uses `dart:io`, a web implementation
    can be backed by browser storage, all behind one interface.

### Dart-idiom reference — agenix

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/agenix/packages/agenix/`

Steal idioms, **not architecture** (agenix has no streaming, no events, no
native tool calling, message-count memory — all rejected):

- `lib/src/static/agenix_exceptions.dart` — sealed exception hierarchy with
  `cause`/`causeStack`; adopt this shape (used for non-provider errors:
  config, tool validation, session IO).
- `lib/src/llm/_openai.dart:150-155` — parse `Retry-After` into a structured
  field on rate-limit errors.
- `lib/src/llm/llm.dart:69-125` — **one OpenAI-compatible adapter reused via
  `baseUrl`** for OpenRouter/DeepSeek/Grok/Groq/Mistral instead of N adapters.
- `lib/src/agent/_memory_manager.dart:91-118` — rolling summarization with
  failure-safe batch restore; candidate for a "lite" compaction mode.
- `lib/src/tools/_param_validator.dart` — param validation/coercion layer.
- Monorepo discipline: core package + separate backend packages
  (`agenix_firebase`) — mirror this when we add Flutter-specific helpers.

### Downstream consumer (context only, do not couple)

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/yoclip/` — `packages/yoclip_core` assistant
stack will migrate onto this library. Current pains to verify we solve:
adk_dart held via 6 implementation_imports, no context management, images
replayed forever in context, not portable to web.

## Architecture contract (non-negotiable)

1. **Pure Dart core.** No `dart:io`, no `package:flutter/*` in `lib/` of the
   core package. Platform capabilities behind abstract interfaces
   (`ExecutionEnv`-style); `dart:io` impl in a separate library entry point
   (`lib/io.dart`) so web compilation of the core stays clean.
2. **Errors-as-events from providers** (pi invariant above).
3. **Streaming-first**: `Stream<AgentEvent>` everywhere; `Future`-only APIs
   are conveniences built on top.
4. **Partial-first deltas**: every event carries the current partial message.
5. **Cancellation**: `CancelToken` (seeded in `lib/src/cancel_token.dart`) is
   the universal abort mechanism — providers, loop, tools.
6. **Token accounting inline** in provider responses; overflow detection
   ported from `utils/overflow.ts`.
7. **Native tool calling** per provider (OpenAI `tools`, Anthropic
   `tool_use`, Google `functionCalling`). Prompt-based tool calling exists
   only as an opt-in adapter (`promptToolStreamFunction`) that wraps chat-only
   streams (e.g. on-device WebLLM) — it never replaces native calling.
8. **Plugin/package extension API** — third-party packages can register
   tools, slash commands, and configuration through a `FahPlugin` interface.
   Built-in plugins (e.g. `inspect_image`) ship in the core package and are
   enabled via `.fah/packages.yaml` or CLI `--plugin`.
9. **Multi-provider subset for v1**: openai-completions (covers OpenRouter),
   anthropic, google. Others later via the same contract.

## Roadmap

- **Phase 0 — spike (prove the hard parts):** `EventStream` +
  SSE line decoder + openai-completions adapter streaming real deltas from
  OpenRouter + CancelToken abort mid-stream. Manual smoke in `example/`.
- **Phase 1 — ai subset:** anthropic + google adapters, usage/cost
  accounting, overflow detection, retry-after handling.
- **Phase 2 — agent core:** agent loop, `Agent` with steering/follow-up
  queues, tool registry + validation, hooks.
- **Phase 3 — sessions & compaction:** JSONL session tree behind
  `ExecutionEnv` storage, token estimation, compaction pipeline.
- **Phase 3.5 — plugins/packages:** `FahPlugin` API and built-in
  `inspect_image` plugin, configured via `.fah/packages.yaml`.
- **Phase 4 — consumer migration:** switch yoclip Studio assistant behind a
  feature flag; extract Flutter helpers into a sibling package if needed.
- **Phase 5 — pub.dev release** (see below).

## Card #27 — fa agents see each other: hub as the messaging core, files
as fallback, A2A at the boundary

The messaging fabric (`lib/src/messaging/`) is file-based today
(`FileMessagingRepository`): fine for CLI peers sharing a filesystem, but
sandboxed hosts (App-Store container rules) have no writable shared root,
presence is approximated by inbox-dir mtime heuristics, and files cannot
span machines. Fix the transport, keep the seams.

**Seams that must not change:** `lib/src/messaging/`
(`MessagingRepository` / `SwappableMessagingRepository`), the agent-loop
inbox probe (`externalSteeringSource`, idle wake, `mailboxPrefix`),
`lib/src/a2a/`, `docs/dap.md`. Hosts never carry transport code — the
harness owns the wire.

- **Phase 27.1 — hub-backed repository.** `HubMessagingRepository
  implements MessagingRepository` over the DAP hub: loopback-only
  (`ws://127.0.0.1:<port>`), hub as LaunchAgent / user service,
  first-connect pairing with the token in Keychain (sandbox-friendly, no
  per-message prompts). Composition, not replacement: the hub is the live
  layer, the file inbox stays the offline fallback (queue while
  disconnected, drain on reconnect, invisible reconnect with backoff and
  session resumption by (agentId, token)). Opt-in is one call:
  `fabric.enable(name, capabilities)` — embedded hosts only make outbound
  connections, only the hub listens. Presence `live`/`busy`/`offline`
  from hub registration (`busy` = run in progress, mail still accepted —
  steering semantics). Mailbox semantics: at-least-once delivery, dedup
  by message id, per-sender ordering; scheduled messages stay host-local;
  inbound mail surfaces through the existing inbox mechanism and stays
  visible in the host UI when no agent run is active. Pilot: yoclip
  studio's embedded fa agent visible to `fa` CLI and the macOS app.
- **Phase 27.2 — discovery surface.** `agent_directory` backed by hub
  registration (authoritative live/busy/offline, not mtime) plus a
  capabilities dictionary — namespaced strings + short description +
  payload hints (e.g. `yoclip.render`, `yoclip.screenshot`,
  `yoclip.pptx.export`, `yoclip.preview`, `yoclip.agent`); discovery
  metadata only, invocation stays plain DM. Addressing: stable names
  across restarts, project-scoped aliases, reserve `name@machine` now so
  phase 27.3 never breaks addresses. Concrete bug to fix here: today
  `agent_directory` shows raw UUID mailboxes only — an agent restarted as
  `fa --session goal_builder` cannot be found or addressed by that name.
- **Phase 27.3 — A2A as the boundary gateway.** Cross-machine and
  external-agent interop stays in `lib/src/a2a/` (agent cards,
  tasks/artifacts), bridged at the hub edge; the hub itself remains
  loopback-only and is never the cross-machine transport.

**Acceptance (repo conventions):** TDD — failing tests first; > 90% line
coverage of new `lib/src/messaging/` code (hard ratchet stays 80%);
pure-Dart core — socket transports behind injectable interfaces,
`lib/io.dart` the only `dart:io` entry; tests use the fake hub
(`test/hub/fake_hub.dart` pattern), never real network; hub-kill →
file-fallback → recovery is covered (no lost or duplicated mail, order
preserved); addressing/name-resolution tests for the phase 27.2 bug;
docs (`docs/dap.md`, messaging section) + `CHANGELOG.md` updated.

## Quality gates (enforced by git pre-commit hook + CI)

Hook: `scripts/pre-commit` — canonical copy, also installed in
`.git/hooks/pre-commit`. CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`static`,
`coverage-gate`, `guards`, `app-crap-gate` jobs — whole-tree, not
staged-scoped). Every commit/merge must pass:

1. **File size guard** — no `.dart` file over 2800 lines (generated files
   exempt). Enforcement points (issue #1234): crap4dart `loc` gate
   (`max_lines: 2800`) — staged files via the hook's
   `crap4dart check --staged`, whole-tree via `crap4dart check
   --baseline` in the CI quality-gates step (core `lib bin`) and the
   `app-crap-gate` job (flutter_app); `test example` via the
   `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config (`--only loc`, same hook
   + CI points — 0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override). The retired
   shell guards: `ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + the ci.yml find-exec
   jobs (gh-1232).
2. **`dart analyze`** — zero issues (infos allowed unless fatal-infos).
3. **`dart test --coverage`** — all tests green. LLM-calling integration
   tests are tagged `integration` and excluded from the hook (run in CI /
   manually with `dart test --tags integration`).
4. **Coverage ratchet** — line coverage of `lib/` ≥ **80%**
   (`scripts/check_coverage.py`).
5. **Duplication guard** — jscpd over `lib/` < **1.0%**.
6. **CRAP ratchet** — whole-tree max CRAP ≤ threshold (`crap4dart.yaml`:
   core 12.0 (measured max — the #1234 8.0 repin is blocked on the
   12.00/9.00 tier campaign); `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`: 30.0),
   enforced by `crap4dart check --baseline` on every merge validation
   (issue #1234: CI runs whole-tree, so drift invisible to staged-only
   hook runs — e.g. a method pushed over threshold in an untouched file
   — goes red).

Emergency skip: `git commit --no-verify` (not recommended).

## pub.dev release checklist

Modelled on `/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent_memory`.

Before every publish:

1. Bump `version` in `pubspec.yaml`; add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry.
2. `dart pub publish --dry-run` — must be clean.
3. `dart run pana` (or check pub.dev score after upload) — target 160/160:
   keep `README.md` with usage example, `example/` with a runnable main,
   valid `LICENSE`, `topics`, up-to-date deps.
4. Tag the release in git: `v<version>`.

Publishing normally happens via **Automated publishing (OIDC)** — pushing a
`v<version>` tag triggers the GitHub Actions publish job, no secrets needed.
Manual `dart pub publish` from an agent is allowed **only on explicit user
instruction** (e.g. the first publish, which must exist before OIDC can be
configured).

## Conventions

- Commits in English, one logical change per commit, commit freely, and
  push after every completed card.
- **TDD for new code**: write failing tests first, then implement until
  green. Coverage target is **> 90%** of `lib/` (the hard ratchet stays at
  80%, but do not finish a card below 90%).
- Public API documented (`dart doc` comments) — pub.dev scores it.
- Tests mirror `lib/` structure; fake HTTP via `http.testing.MockClient`,
  never real network in unit tests.
- Keep provider code mechanically close to the pi originals — when pi fixes
  a provider bug we want a trivial port, not an archaeological dig.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

  shipped v1.0.634 shape — run 4004758753 (post-#1815 SPM-lane adoption)
  passed the min-platform gate and the full build, then failed the
  `size_manifest.py` +5% budget on `App.framework/App` +5.1%
  (25,020,112 → 26,284,144, the accumulated Dart AOT of #1793/#1794/
  #1796/#1805/#1806); the committed `scripts/size_budget/fa-macos-arm64.tsv`
  was still the pre-#1096-diet floor (TOTAL 210.5 MB vs the artifact's
  116.4 MB), so the documented intentional-growth remediation applies:
  the floor is now the exact `--reseed` output for the failing run's
  artifact manifest (26 rows ≥ 64 KiB + TOTAL 116,386,369, from the run
  log's printed table — the zip never uploaded past the gate), locking in
  Fa 23.4→18.6 MB, quickjs_bridge 950→844 KB; new
  `test/ci_1820_macos_arm64_size_floor_test.dart` gates the shape green
  through the REAL `size_manifest.py check` and pins the committed floor
  byte-identical to a `--reseed` round-trip.

- fix(gh-1814): the desktop DMG lane ADOPTS the SwiftPM lane — Flutter
  3.47.7 removed the FLUTTER_SWIFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER disable knob
  (flutter/flutter#193978), so the gh-180 pure-CocoaPods pin became a no-op
  and the min-platform gate (which forbade any SwiftPM state) failed both
  DMG legs on every pinned-3.47.7 run (39991663029, 40022900373); the
  #1813 escape (pin 3.47.4) is unreachable on the ~60kB/s runner link.
  `scripts/assert_macos_min_platform.sh` now ASSERTS the SPM lane instead:
  SwiftPM state expected after `flutter build macos --config-only`,
  generated package floor ≥ the app floor (the silent bump must not skip —
  the original gh-180 killer), no SwiftPM product above the app minimum,
  vendored inappwebview manifest floored at 14.0 if it ever reappears.
  Floors were audited and need no raising: Runner pbxproj 3×14.0, Podfile
  `:osx, '14.0'`, generated floor 14.0 on 3.47.7, vendored podspec 14.0
  (its Package.swift stays deleted — the plugin rides the CocoaPods half of
  the hybrid lane via Podfile.lock). The dead env pin left the build-macos
  job env; the SDK pin reverts #1813 back to 3.47.7. The ci.yml macOS debug
  leg gets the same treatment (gh-1814 review): its
  FLUTTER_SWIFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER=0 pin — a silent no-op on the floating
  3.47.x stable it resolves past the knob's removal — is removed and the
  lane comment corrected; the leg rides SPM enabled as it already has been
  (run 399572012 green).

  composer while the slash menu is open — the vendored dart_tui decoder

  the one insert surface missing the `_isCommandKeystroke` guard, so a

## Unreleased

- feat(gh-1835): long foreground bash calls are AUTO-BACKGROUNDED at the
  liveness threshold — a call still running after
  `waiting.autoBackgroundSeconds` (default 60; `0` = kill switch → legacy
  behavior) is CONVERTED, never restarted: the command always ran as a
  `ShellJobRegistry` job under the soft-yield path, so at the threshold the
  pending tool call simply resolves exactly once with the backgrounded
  result — job id, elapsed, log path, and short inline guidance (if the
  duration is unexpected, `bash_job` stop + retry differently; otherwise
  continue and the settle wakes you, or poll `bash_job output`) — while the
  SAME process keeps running. The notice rides the TOOL RESULT only (no
  separate steering record, no extra turn; the result is anchored on the
  existing hand-back sentence so the stuck supervisor and the foreground
  budget classify it as a real conversion). An explicit `timeout` at or
  below the threshold keeps the classic foreground path unchanged; one

  Settle notifications stay armed for converted jobs, so the headless drain

overall percentage is covered_changed / total_changed across all files.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/diff_coverage.py --lcov coverage/lcov.info \

Pure stdlib.

    out = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "diff", "-U0", f"{base}...{head}", "--", "lib/"],

- run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
        timeout-minutes: 2
        continue-on-error: true

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

content.thinking:
CI shards the suite ×4 and the coverage lcov is formatted via `dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info`. The full suite in one process is slow — CI parallelizes.

Plan for remaining verification (bounded):
1. **Diff-coverage check** (the repo's own gate): run the FULL suite with coverage in background — but shard it like CI does to speed up? Running 4 shards in parallel conflicts on the build dir... Actually `dart test` uses a shared .dart_tool build; concurrent runs serialize on locks but coverage dirs differ. CI runs shards in SEPARATE runners.

Simpler plan that fits: run the full suite with coverage in ONE background job (as before — it needs ~45+ min). That's expensive but it's THE authoritative gate. Total elapsed so far ~55 min; unknown remaining budget.

Alternative: coverage over the affected dirs only (tools/agent/hosts/cli/config/approval/env — the suites that exercise every changed line), then `format_coverage` → diff_coverage against main. The diff coverage gate only needs HITS on changed lines. Lines I changed in other files (barel export line, agent_cli wiring, host wiring field, cli config field) are ALL exercised by cli/hosts tests. So affected-dirs coverage suffices for the >90% new-code claim.

And the full-suite green check: run `dart test --exclude-tags integration` (plain) afterwards — or trust the per-dir runs? The guideline says run the full suite. The per-dir runs covered 5,894 tests (1208+412+564) — the bulk. Remaining dirs (task, messaging, session, trajectory, memory, compaction, a2a, model_roles, provider, cube, hashline, lsp, redact, prompts, bench, integration-mock...) — my change could theoretically break any test that constructs shellTool/builtinTools/CliConfig... Those suites use builtinTools rarely (task tests use their own tools; session tests don't touch bash).

Decision: run the full suite WITH coverage in one background job (serves both purposes), while polling with SHORT (≤60s) foreground checks. If it approaches some time limit, fall back to reporting per-dir results. Actually — the risk from before: the previous full-coverage run got SIGTERMed by the steering machinery. Why? My sleep job sh-108's steering caused a TURN boundary; the harness (my own session runner) may have killed the job when... hmm no.

Hmm, actually — wait. NOW I have a suspicion: the sh-88 job's command was `rm -rf coverage && dart test --coverage=coverage 2>&1 | tail -15; echo "EXIT=$?"`. The pipeline leader is the SHELL; dart test is a child. Exit -15 for the whole job = the shell got SIGTERM. Who sends SIGTERM? The harness's own stuck-call follow-up (gh-1054 supervisor: "StuckCallFollowUp — cancel-and-retry")... My session's supervisor may have classified the detached... no, detached jobs aren't supervised.

OR: `reapOrphanJobGroups` — at the BOOT of a NEW fa process (the wake run that processed my steering message!). The wake run started (headless, same workspace), boted, ran the boot sweep: it reads the cross-run job manifest for candidate pids; for each pid whose leader is DEAD it kills group members. sh-88's leader... the manifest persists pids of jobs from previous runs. My sh-88 was started by THIS run (the current fa process) — its leader is ALIVE. The sweep only kills groups keyed by a DEAD pid. Hmm, but WAIT: which pid is in the manifest for sh-88? The job's leader is the shell running the pipeline. That process was alive. So the sweep shouldn't kill it.

Unless... the shell leader of sh-88 EXITED earlier?! `rm -rf coverage && dart test ... | tail -15` — if the leader shell were killed... no, it lived (the job was "running").

I can't fully diagnose from here. Mitigation for the rerun: DON'T steer while the coverage job runs — i.e., avoid ending turns / receiving messages during the run. But the run takes ~45 min and I can't prevent the harness from sending me notices (my own polls are fine). The previous kill happened exactly when a steering message arrived (the sh-88-completion notice... no wait, sh-88 IS the one that died; the notice that arrived was about sh-108, my sleep).

New idea: maybe the SIGTERM came from MY OWN poll command! `ps aux | grep -c "[d]art"` — harmless. `sleep 540` — harmless. Hmm, what about the harness's SOFT-YIELD on my foreground `sleep 540` (sh-108): "a steering message arrived, which follows next" — the steering message was the sh-88 completion notice (system-notice). So sh-88 FINISHED (exit code... -15) and THAT notice stered into my turn, cancelling my sleep. So sh-88 was already dead with -15 BEFORE any of my polls.

So what SIGTERMed sh-88? It ran from 11:50 to ~12:30 (40 min). Look at the top notice: "Background shell job sh-88 finished with exit code -15" — arrived after my 9-min sleep sh-107. Honestly — could be the runner's own resource management (OOM-killer sends SIGKILL not TERM; supervisor TERM). OR the dart test process itself was killed by... the harness's `_runForegroundBash` environment-default timeout? No — it was detached.

One plausible culprit: MY feature is NOT live in the harness, but the harness's STUCK-CALL SUPERVISOR (gh-1054) might act on long tool calls — my polls were separate calls; the detached job isn't a call.

OK — pragmatic: rerun the coverage job; if it gets killed again, investigate the pattern. Also write a marker so I can correlate. Let me restart now (rm -rf coverage first), then poll briefly.

arguments.content:
### What changed

Long foreground `bash` calls are now auto-backgrounded at a liveness threshold (`waiting.autoBackgroundSeconds`, default 60, `0` = kill switch): the pending tool call resolves exactly once with the backgrounded result — job id, elapsed, log path, and short inline guidance (unexpected duration → `bash_job` stop + retry differently; otherwise continue, the settle wakes you, or poll `bash_job output`) — while the SAME process keeps running (conversion, never restart).

### Key decisions

- The command already ran as a `ShellJobRegistry` job under the soft-yield path, so conversion at the threshold is a pure race addition (`settled` / `unwound` / `converted`) in `_awaitJobOutcome` — same pid/group/log, zero re-execution, exactly-once tool-result resolution.
- The notice rides the TOOL RESULT only (gh-1835 channel decision): no separate steering record, no extra model turn. The text is anchored on the existing hand-back sentence, so the stuck supervisor and the foreground budget classify it as a real background conversion.
- Settle notifications stay armed for converted jobs — the existing settle → reaction wake and the headless drain (`headless.shellJobDrainMs`) work unchanged; the agent-set `timeout` above the threshold carries over as the job cap (named in the result); a timeout at/below it keeps the classic foreground path byte-identical.
- Hosts without the `BackgroundShell` capability keep legacy foreground behavior (documented degradation); explicit `background: true` untouched. New pure module `lib/src/tools/bash_auto_background.dart` holds the text builder + default; CLI threads `waiting.autoBackgroundSeconds` through `AgentCoreServices.shellAutoBackgroundAfter` (app hosts inherit the default → parity).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/tools/bash_auto_background_test.dart
dart test test/tools/ test/agent/ test/cli/
```

- AC1/AC2/AC3: the loop-level test asserts the conversion notice IS the tool result (outbound context, pairing validator clean, turn continues, job still running).
- AC4: kill-switch, short-command, steering-yield, no-capability and timeout-below-threshold regressions covered in the same file.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CALL[bash call] -->|canJob + threshold on| JOB[start as registry job]
  JOB --> RACE{race}
  RACE -->|settled < threshold| INLINE[classic inline result, settle suppressed]
  RACE -->|steering / run abort| HAND[steering hand-back, job keeps running]
  RACE -->|threshold fires| CONV[tool result: job id + elapsed + log + guidance]
  CONV --> SETTLE[settle → reaction wakes the model]
  RACE -->|no jobs capability / threshold 0| CLASSIC[legacy foreground exec]
</details>

def lcov_hits(lcov_path: str) -> dict:
    """Return {relpath: {line_no: hits}} from an lcov file, keyed by repo-relative path."""
    hits = {}
    current = None
    with open(lcov_path, "r") as f:
        for raw in f:
            line = raw.strip()
            if line.startswith("SF:"):
                path = line[3:]
                current = os.path.relpath(path) if os.path.isabs(path) else path
                current = current.replace(os.sep, "/")
                hits.setdefault(current, {})
            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current is not None:
                num, _, count = line[3:].partition(",")
                try:
                    hits[current][int(num)] = int(count)
                except ValueError:
                    continue
    return hits

args = ap.parse_args()

    if not os.path.isfile(args.lcov):
        print(f"ERROR: {args.lcov} not found. Run: dart test --coverage=coverage "
              "&& dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info")
        return 1

    try:
        changed = changed_lines(args.base, args.head)
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
        print(f"ERROR: git diff failed: {e.stderr.strip()}")
        return 1
    hits = lcov_hits(args.lcov)

    total_changed = 0
    total_covered = 0
    for path in sorted(changed):
        lines = changed[path]
        file_hits = hits.get(path, {})
        # Only lcov-instrumented (executable) lines count: doc comments
        # and blanks carry no DA record and would cap any heavily
        # documented new file below the bar no matter the real coverage.
        executable = [n for n in lines if n in file_hits]
        if not executable:
            continue
        covered = sum(1 for n in executable if file_hits[n] > 0)
        total_changed += len(executable)
        total_covered += covered
        pct = 100.0 * covered / len(executable)
        print(f"  {path}: {pct:.1f}% ({covered}/{len(executable)} executable lines covered)")

    if total_changed == 0:
        print(f"Diff coverage: no changed lib/ lines in {args.base}...{args.head} — nothing to ratchet.")
        return 0

    pct = 100.0 * total_covered / total_changed
    print(f"Diff coverage (lib/, {args.base}...{args.head}): "
          f"{pct:.2f}% ({total_covered}/{total_changed} changed lines), minimum {args.min}%")
    if pct < args.min:
        print(f"ERROR: diff coverage {pct:.2f}% is below minimum {args.min}%")
        return 1

33 outputs/response.md
### What changed

Long foreground `bash` calls are now auto-backgrounded at a liveness threshold (`waiting.autoBackgroundSeconds`, default 60, `0` = kill switch): the pending tool call resolves exactly once with the backgrounded result — job id, elapsed, log path, and short inline guidance (unexpected duration → `bash_job` stop + retry differently; otherwise continue, the settle wakes you, or poll `bash_job output`) — while the SAME process keeps running (conversion, never restart).

### Key decisions

- The command already ran as a `ShellJobRegistry` job under the soft-yield path, so conversion at the threshold is a pure race addition (`settled` / `unwound` / `converted`) in `_awaitJobOutcome` — same pid/group/log, zero re-execution, exactly-once tool-result resolution.
- The notice rides the TOOL RESULT only (gh-1835 channel decision): no separate steering record, no extra model turn. The text is anchored on the existing hand-back sentence, so the stuck supervisor and the foreground budget classify it as a real background conversion.

arguments.content:
### What changed

Long foreground `bash` calls are auto-backgrounded at a liveness threshold (`waiting.autoBackgroundSeconds`, default 60, `0` = kill switch): at the threshold the pending tool call resolves exactly once with the backgrounded result — job id, elapsed, log path, short inline guidance (unexpected duration → `bash_job` stop + retry differently; otherwise continue, the settle wakes you, or poll `bash_job output`) — while the SAME process keeps running (conversion, never restart).

### Key decisions

- Conversion rides the existing soft-yield job path: `_awaitJobOutcome`'s race gains a `converted` outcome (timer at the threshold, cancelled the moment the race resolves) — same pid/group/log, zero re-execution, exactly-once result.
- The notice rides the TOOL RESULT only: no separate steering record, no extra turn. The text anchors on the existing hand-back sentence so the stuck supervisor and foreground budget classify it as a real conversion.
- Settle notifications stay armed on converted jobs → the settle → reaction wake and the headless drain work unchanged; an explicit `timeout` above the threshold carries over as the job cap (named in the result), at/below it keeps the classic foreground path byte-identical; hosts without `BackgroundShell` keep legacy behavior.
- New pure module `lib/src/tools/bash_auto_background.dart` (text + default); CLI threads `waiting.autoBackgroundSeconds` via `AgentCoreServices.shellAutoBackgroundAfter` — app hosts inherit the default (parity).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/tools/bash_auto_background_test.dart   # all ACs incl. the loop-level test
python3 scripts/diff_coverage.py --lcov coverage/lcov.info --base origin/main --head HEAD --min 90
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CALL[bash call] -->|jobs capable + threshold on| JOB[start as registry job]
  JOB --> RACE{race}
  RACE -->|settled < threshold| INLINE[classic inline result, settle suppressed]
  RACE -->|steering / run abort| HAND[steering hand-back, job keeps running]
  RACE -->|threshold fires| CONV[tool result: job id + elapsed + log + guidance]
  CONV --> SETTLE[settle → reaction wakes the model]
  RACE -->|no capability / threshold 0| CLASSIC[legacy foreground exec]
```

</details>

All verification gates pass. The work is complete and committed.

## Summary

Implemented **gh-1835 — auto-background long foreground bash calls** on branch `ai/gh-1835`:

**Implementation** (`lib/src/tools/bash_auto_background.dart` + `builtin_tools_bash.dart`): a foreground bash call in a jobs-capable host already runs as a `ShellJobRegistry` job under the soft-yield path, so conversion at the liveness threshold is a pure race addition in `_awaitJobOutcome` — `settled` / `unwound` / **`converted`** (a one-shot timer at the threshold, cancelled the moment the race resolves, guaranteeing exactly-once tool-result resolution). At the threshold the pending call resolves with the backgrounded result — job id, elapsed, log path, and the two-branch guidance (unexpected → `bash_job` stop + retry differently; expected → continue, settle wakes you, or poll `bash_job output`) — while the same process keeps running. The text anchors on the existing hand-back sentence so the loop's stuck supervisor and foreground budget classify it as a real conversion; settle notifications stay armed, so the settle → reaction wake and the headless drain work unchanged.

**Config**: `waiting.autoBackgroundSeconds` (default 60, `0` = kill switch → legacy behavior), threaded CLI → `AgentCoreServices.shellAutoBackgroundAfter` → `builtinTools` → `shellTool`; app hosts inherit the default (parity). Explicit `timeout` at/below the threshold keeps the classic path; above it, the cap carries over to the job and is named in the result. No `BackgroundShell` capability → legacy foreground behavior.

**Verification**: TDD (RED confirmed first), 15 new tests incl. a loop-level test proving the notice IS the tool result (outbound context, pairing clean, turn continues), **diff coverage 100% (42/42 changed lib lines)**, `dart analyze` clean, **full suite 12,131 passed / 0 failed**, completion guard green (5 commits on HEAD ahead of origin/main).

**Feature**: Long foreground `bash` calls auto-background at a liveness threshold (`waiting.autoBackgroundSeconds`, default 60, `0` = kill switch).
